questionText:
[Q1] Statements:
1. All mangoes are golden in color.
2. No golden-colored things are cheap.
Conclusions:
I. All mangoes are cheap.
II. Golden-colored mangoes are not cheap. (Options: Only II follows, Only I follows...)
explanation: Since no golden-colored things are cheap and all mangoes are golden, no mangoes are cheap. Hence, Conclusion II follows.

questionText:
[Q2] Statements:
1. Some dogs are barkers.
2. All barkers are biting animals.
Conclusions:
I. Some dogs are biting animals.
II. Some biting animals are dogs. (Options: Both I and II follow, Only I follows...)
explanation: Some dogs -> barkers -> biting animals. So some dogs are biting animals (I follows). By conversion, some biting animals are dogs (II follows). Both follow.

questionText:
[Q3] Statements:
1. All cups are plates.
2. All plates are spoons.
Conclusions:
I. All cups are spoons.
II. All spoons are cups. (Options: Only I follows, Only II follows...)
explanation: All A are B and All B are C implies All A are C. So All cups are spoons (I follows). But All spoons are cups does not necessarily follow.

[Q4] Statements:

2. All books are papers.
Conclusions:
I. Some pens are papers.
II. No pen is a paper. (Options: Only I follows, Only II follows...)
explanation: Some pens are books and All books are papers => Some pens are papers (I follows). II contradicts I.

2. All bats are mammals.
Conclusions:
I. No bat is a bird.
II. No bird is a bat. (Options: Both I and II follow, Only I follows...)
explanation: Bats are entirely inside mammals, and mammals have zero intersection with birds. Thus no bat is a bird and no bird is a bat. Both follow.
